final_rationale: The verdict remains noncompliant. The Actor did not provide new admissible evidence; the response narrowed the claim and accurately conceded the same core gaps already identified in the record. That reframing does not satisfy the policy predicate. Under the policy text, certification may proceed only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by an approved mitigation. The admissible evidence still shows a current subgroup regression 1.3 percentage points below the warning threshold, and it still does not show attached current disclosure language, approved mitigation, or approved risk acceptance. Aggregate readiness and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness, but they do not cure the missing documentation and disclosure requirement. This is therefore not merely a caveated presentation issue; the caveat itself is an unresolved compliance condition.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows current release documentation reflects the current evaluation results.
No admissible evidence shows the material public-records-triage weakness is disclosed in the current certification packet.
No admissible evidence shows an approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance covering the subgroup weakness before launch.
Prior approval predates the retrieval configuration change and current evaluation batch, so it cannot satisfy the current-release policy predicate.
The informal post-launch monitoring comment is not reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or attached disclosure language.
